etymologies.etymologyHTML: From pre- +‎ view; compare Old French preveü, past participle of preveoir (“to foresee”).

definitions.definition: An experience of something in advance.

quote.citation: 2013 June 7, David Simpson, “Fantasy of navigation”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 188, number 26, page 36:
quote.text: It is tempting to speculate about the incentives or compulsions that might explain why anyone would take to the skies in [the] basket [of a balloon]: perhaps out of a desire to escape the gravity of this world or to get a preview of the next; […].

definitions.definition: (colloquial) An advance showing of a film, exhibition etc.
Something seen in advance. (Can we add an example for this sense?)
(computing) A facility for viewing and checking a document or photo, or changes to it, before saving or printing it.
(transitive) To show or watch something, or part of it, before it is complete.

quote.citation: 1991 August 24, Lewis Gannett, “Gore Stories”, in Gay Community News, volume 19, number 6, page 8:
quote.text: Vidal's talk was caled "The Screening Of History," and it was a free-ranging meditation on the United States, the movies, on Vidal's personal history and numerous interconnections. (It also previewed a forthcoming book by the same name.)

definitions.definition: (computing, transitive) To show something in advance, a facility for viewing and checking a document or photo, or changes to it, before saving or printing it.
